Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The broken video box on the GlasgowLive article is a Primis video advertising player that Base filter rule ||live.primis.tech^$third-party blocks; site-scoped allowlists of live.primis.tech and of all primis.tech both failed to restore playback (the ad stack is also blocked), so no acceptable rule exists and the report needs a maintainer decision.

## Still visible after the rule

- Embedded storm video player below byline/timestamp, above article body — Player shows only a still flooded-street poster with a play overlay and black caption bar reading 'STORM BOELO:⁠ DRAMATIC FOOTAGE OF FLOODED LARGS MAIN STREET - FOOTAGE BY GERALDO'S'; no playing video footage is visible.
- Article body, large grey media box below the 'Ayrshire appears...' paragraph and above the caption 'Geraldo's owner said the scenes at the shop were a disaster...' — Large empty grey rectangle where an article image/gallery should render; only the 'View 2 Images' button is visible, with no image content.
- Article body near bottom, below the 'Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT' divider and the Tha-Tien-Thai paragraphs — Large blank grey media/image placeholder begins at the lower edge; no image content is visible in the box.
- Article center column, media/video area directly below byline and timestamp, captioned 'STORM BOELO:⁠ DRAMATIC FOOTAGE OF FLOODED LARGS MAIN STREET - FOOTAGE BY GERALDO'S' — Large media/video area shows only a nighttime flood poster image with a centered circular loading spinner; no video frame or playback is visible.

### Add your comment and screenshots

The content on the website is not clickable/selectable due to the presence of `gcs-cc-lock` class on `<html>`, causing the `html.gcs-cc-lock body::before` rule to cover the page with a transparent `::before` pseudo-element. The `gcs-cc-lock` class is usually removed by accepting the cookie consent. However, since the consent is removed by the following rule, that does not occur: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c674b6c7e2d7f265e5f12d7e9c06df5f750724d5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_general.txt#L272

Adding `globalcitizensolutions.com##+js(remove-class, gcs-cc-lock, html)` effectively avoids the issue.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"ebad3929d29d1fe2d275ae64c644a14ca16bd1b010e4186da85c25aa3ab12f65"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Genuine filter false positive:⁠ `###moove_gdpr_cookie_info_bar` (Cookies filter, cookies_general.txt:⁠272) hides the Moov consent bar, so the theme never clears `gcs-cc-lock` from `<html>` and its fixed `body::before` overlay plus `body{overflow:hidden}` make every link unclickable and the page unscrollable (verified:⁠ elementFromPoint returns BODY, scrollY stays 0). The evidence-backed fix `globalcitizensolutions.com#%#//scriptlet('remove-class', 'gcs-cc-lock', 'html')` (cookies_specific.txt) removed the class in the candidate phase but the vision review rejected it for blank lower-page tiles that are equally blank with no filtering at all, so it stays unverified.

## Still visible after the rule

- Citizenship by Investment / Residency by Investment — Entire tile is a blank white region with no visible page content; the Citizenship by Investment and Residency by Investment content that should appear here is absent.
- Residency by Investment / A Global Perspective — Entire tile is a blank white region with no visible page content; the Residency by Investment and A Global Perspective content that should appear here is absent.
- A Global Perspective / As Featured In Top Global Media — Entire tile is a blank white region with no visible page content; the A Global Perspective and As Featured In Top Global Media content that should appear here is absent.
- Entire viewport (header, hero, and first lower section) — Uniform dimming/gating overlay spanning the whole viewport, covering the header, hero content, buttons, and lower page content; matches the reported full-page gcs-cc-lock overlay that blocks interaction.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's blank region on news.jp is an empty fundit/GPT ad slot:⁠ a class-less wrapper with inline min-height 250px between the もっと見る button and the あなたにおすすめ heading (plus two more 50px wrappers below the header and at the page bottom). Hiding those wrappers with news.jp#⁠#⁠div:⁠has(⁠> .fundit-ad-placeholder) removed all 350px of blank space; the CLI-proxy A/B/C experiment returned verified with the symptom resolved, no remaining instances and page integrity intact. ## Rule `news.jp##div:has(> .fundit-ad-placeholder)` ## Policy rationale The run instruction states no rule that closes this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising (the empty slots are third-party fundit/GPT ad containers), not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall. The report is an ordinary ad-filtering defect (leftover empty ad slot), so a filter-list rule may be generated. ## Place in the list [MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1b0ab187d67164bb0ea132deb753599bee955e86/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 666](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1b0ab187d67164bb0ea132deb753599bee955e86/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt#L666). ## Screenshots

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The "ads" on tftacademy.com's comp page are the site's own bundled self-promotion:⁠ the circled left panel is two 300x250 house-ad creatives for TFT Academy's Overlay tool and Academy+ membership (internal /overlay and /academyplus links), the wide slot shows an empty "AD" placeholder, and no third-party ad or detector request exists in the HAR. Filter policy says the site's own advertising gets no rule, so the report is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction / AdGuard filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter's annotated target and every other ad placement observed on the page are the site's own bundled self-promotion (creatives linking to /overlay and /academyplus), not third-party advertising. Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules" - no deliberate blocking rule is warranted here. Filter policy on ad-block detection messages:⁠ they are not blocked when they "allow the usage of the website and do not overlay the significant amount of content"; the only 'disable ad block' wording seen is baked into a first-party 300x250 creative that does not gate or overlay content, and the captured requests contain no detector script (no third-party host at all), so the instruction's anti-adblock branch ("write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script") is not met. The agent never closes an issue; this outcome only recommends closing for a maintainer to decide.

issue.title: ad-contents.jp: Ponta kanji and idiom quiz anti-adblock gates (path-scoped workaround)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Current retest status — 14 October 2026 (JST)

**The AdGuard Japanese filter was ENABLED and verified during the retests (version 2.0.77.44).** All five custom document exceptions were disabled for the initial comparisons; the later original-Japanese tests had Google Translate disabled.

- Kanji/idiom first-question access and Resort wall/menu access worked without their exceptions; those three exceptions were removed.
- **Paw remains unresolved:** with protection ON, the normal bonus-ad page stayed loading through approximately 65 seconds; with protection OFF, normal ad completion and bonus entry worked. The retained Paw exception is still unverified because a fresh eligible ad is required.
- The separate English vocabulary game is tracked in [#222607](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/222607#issuecomment-6148987274). Its gate disappeared with only the built-in AdGuard DNS filter disabled and returned when that filter was restored. The exact hostname/rule is unknown.

The original “Japanese disabled” and Chrome 140 entries below describe the historical initial report; the dated retests and installed Chrome 155.0.8059.39 correction supersede them. The Japanese-filter question was already answered in [the earlier follow-up](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/244149#issuecomment-6150655951) and is answered again in [this direct reply](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/244149#issuecomment-6157738716).

---

### Issue URL (AdGuard gets detected / website unavailable)

- https://ad-contents.jp/kanji/ponta/
- https://ad-contents.jp/yojijukugo/ponta/

These are the Ponta PLAY kanji and four-character idiom quizzes. Account-specific query parameters have been omitted.

### Description

On 13 October 2026, both pages displayed this gate instead of the quiz:

> This content cannot be accessed if AdBlock is enabled. Please disable AdBlock and try accessing it again.

I want to allow the advertisements on these particular games while keeping filtering enabled for unrelated websites.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open https://play.ponta.jp/content_list/index.html using an existing Ponta PLAY account.
2. Choose Pontaの漢字テスト or Pontaの四字熟語クイズ.
3. Observe the gate above before reaching the game.
4. Apply the exact site/path exception below and reopen the same game through the content list.
5. Compare the visible result with the baseline.

### Narrow exception and retest

- Kanji rule: `@@|https://ad-contents.jp/kanji/ponta/$document`
- Idiom rule: `@@|https://ad-contents.jp/yojijukugo/ponta/$document`
- Kanji after fresh navigation: rules and quiz load; question/answer flow works.
- Idiom after fresh navigation to its actual route: introduction and start route load; the AdBlock gate is gone.
- Kanji game access is restored with the scoped exception. The responsible upstream filter has not been isolated.
- Idiom introduction/start access is restored. Completed idiom play or reward credit is not asserted.
- Global protection remains enabled; both exception rules listed above were saved and read back enabled.
- Specific responsible upstream filter: not isolated.

### System configuration

| Field | Observed value / verification status |
| --- | --- |
| AdGuard product / version | AdGuard for Android 4.14.2 (build 42220003) |
| Android version | 16 |
| Browser / version | Chrome 140.0.7339.207 |
| Observed enabled public filters - partial list | AdGuard Base filter, AdGuard Mobile Ads filter, AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, AdGuard Popups filter, AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter, AdGuard Other Annoyances filter, AdGuard Widgets filter, Adblock Warning Removal List, Fanboy's Annoyances, AdGuard Social Media filter, AdGuard Russian filter |
| Observed regional filter note | Russian enabled; Japanese disabled |
| Filter update time | Not verified |
| Relevant HTTPS / DNS filtering | Not verified in supplied readback |
| Global AdGuard protection | Enabled before and after these path-specific changes |

### Comparison and limitations

Global AdGuard protection was not disabled for a comparison. This comparison used the two path-specific exceptions listed above. Product/browser currency and filter-update timing have not been independently verified. The public filter names are the visible readbacks, not a complete private configuration export.

### Related report

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/52566 was resolved in March 2020 for /quiz/ponta/. This report concerns the currently reproduced /kanji/ponta/ and /yojijukugo/ponta/ routes.

### Screenshot description

The saved baseline captures show the quoted AdBlock gate on each game landing page. Fresh retest captures show accessible kanji quiz and actual idiom introduction/start routes. No screenshot attachment has been uploaded. The visible gate and reproduction steps are described above; account-specific information is omitted.


Could you investigate a narrowly scoped compatibility fix for these two quiz paths? The workaround restores access while global protection stays enabled; the responsible upstream filter has not been isolated.

========================================================================


---

### Consolidated retest — 14 October 2026 (JST)

Following the maintainer's consolidation request, this update covers #244150 and #244151 alongside the original quizzes.

**Configuration:** AdGuard Japanese filter enabled, version **2.0.77.44**, displayed update **13 October 2026, 23:35 JST**. All five temporary document exceptions were disabled and checked before testing. The later tests used original Japanese, Google Translate disabled and Japanese first in Chrome's languages. Chrome remained muted with its per-app audio-focus operation set to ignore; these audio settings were unchanged between the Paw comparisons.

Fresh original-Japanese retests after disabling translation also reached **第1問** on both routes with protection enabled. Full quiz completion, advertisements and reward credit were not tested.

**Resort (#244151):** normal entry with protection enabled and its exception disabled reached the original-Japanese wall and contents menu; a promotional overlay could be dismissed. This verifies wall/menu access, not every individual game or advertisement.

**Paw (#244150), protection enabled:** after 18 remaining ordinary rounds without reload, index counter 0 → Next → `already.php` → **動画を見る** → `movie.php` remained **loading** at entry, about 30 seconds and about 65 seconds, without a playback/completion control.

**Paw protection-off baseline:** the disabled state was verified, then fresh normal entry through the same route showed **広告を見る！**. It opened an actual advertiser card with a video panel. At about 30 seconds, **報酬を獲得しました** and the close × appeared. Closing returned **おやつをゲットする！**, which opened `oyatsu_index.php` / **おやつモード**. The normal advertisement-completion and bonus-entry flow therefore worked with protection disabled under the otherwise unchanged stated settings. The responsible filter/module remains unisolated. Protection was restored and verified enabled afterward.

**English vocabulary:** a later original-Japanese retest with protection enabled again showed its blocking AdBlock modal. @@||ponta.content-lump.net/wall.php$document

Retained and re-enabled these two after the comparisons; their presence is not a claim that they reliably fix the failures:

```text

```

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The annotated "SHOCK VPN" banner on adblock.turtlecute.org reproduces, but it is the site's own first-party sponsored placement (inline markup with a data-URI creative, the site's own click tracking, no ad-network request, and it just hides itself when clicked), so repository policy keeps the site's own advertising unblocked and no rule is proposed.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." Filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md, Ad blocking filters ⁠> Limitations and exceptions):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." The reported banner is not suppressed by any general rule, and it is served by the site itself. The agent never closes an issue:⁠ this is a recommendation for a maintainer to check and decide.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40260686421

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On tvtropes.org the reported "Please allow ads on our site or subscribe" wall did not appear on the home page or on three article pages loaded with the reporter's filter set; the page's client-side ad-block detector is already suppressed by the existing AdGuard Base filter scriptlet `tvtropes.org#%#//scriptlet('prevent-setTimeout', '/googletagmanager|offsetHeight|\(\);/')`. Recommend closing as not reproduced, noting the reporter's iOS/Safari execution model could not be exercised here.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule blocks rule generation for this report:⁠ it is an anti-adblock wall on a non-German site, and the run instruction's policy gate for such walls (a rule only when the captured requests show the detector script) was never triggered because no rule was written. Rule generation was unnecessary:⁠ the reporter-defined defect (the "Please allow ads on our site or subscribe" wall replacing article content) was absent on every reported page loaded live with the reporter's filter set.

issue.title: www.integraconsultores.com.ar

labels.name: T: Incorrect Blocking
labels.description: Website or app not working properly due to filtering

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://www.integraconsultores.com.ar/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.integraconsultores.com.ar%2F)

### Comment
> The domains integraconsultores.com.ar and www.integraconsultores.com.ar are blocked by AdGuard DNS as "malicious / phishing" (block page: "Access blocked by AdGuard DNS: Dangerous website"). I believe this is a false positive.
> 
> The site is the legitimate website of an Argentine consulting company (valuation and inventory of fixed assets).
> 
> Steps to reproduce:
> 1. Use the AdGuard DNS public servers (default): 94.140.14.14
> 2. Open https://www.integraconsultores.com.ar/
> 3. The block page is shown. A DNS lookup returns 94.140.14.33 (AdGuard block IP) instead of the real IP 67.227.154.94.
> 
> Checks done:
> - The domain resolves normally through Cloudflare 1.1.1.2, Quad9, OpenDNS and CleanBrowsing Security.
> - It is not listed in AdGuard DNS filter, Phishing Army, URLhaus, Dandelion Sprout anti-malware or Scam blocklist.
> - Sucuri SiteCheck (2026-10-26): no malware, no blacklists.
> 
> Please review it and remove the domain from the malicious/phishing database. Thank you!



### Screenshots
<details>
  <summary>Screenshot 1</summary>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/5e62nib8c28848o48ww04oo0c0kokckev24820k4eo.jpg?nc=1)
</details>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/iml76863an4gwsw8kk04448skgos48wc16lw3hfbf4.jpg?nc=1)

System version: | `Android`

Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"0d0878d4157d78acc9abe57d251197bf1f8f37b66045fb37eefe8cf02b9e89ad"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The video ad shown when selecting a live stream on serenotv.com is the site's own pre-roll:⁠ its inventory is hardcoded in the site's HTML (PREROLL_POOL, is_admin) and its click-through goes to the site's own /pandora/ teaser page, so under the run's filter policy for first-party advertising no rule should be written and I recommend closing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported video ad is a pre-roll defined inside serenotv.com's own served HTML (`const PREROLL_POOL`) with `is_admin: true` and a single hardcoded entry whose click-through goes to the site's own launch-teaser page https:⁠//serenotv.com/pandora/ — the site's own advertising, so no filter rule is generated. Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue. 'Recommend closing' below means the report says no rule is needed; a maintainer checks it and decides." This outcome therefore only recommends closing; the maintainer makes the decision. The same policy also states "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules" — nothing is unblocked here, since no AdGuard rule currently touches the pre-roll (search_rules found no serenotv.com rules and no rule for cdn.videy.co).

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40275355747

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `52dbbe4`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"04cafcda334ea881682be3164801f386eb55979a5734437c458cc1cb8d4e482a"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported block of the bandaancha.eu forum thread did not reproduce:⁠ through the CLI filtering proxy with AdGuard Base + Mobile Ads applied, the thread URL and the site homepage both loaded (HTTP 200) with content rendered, and the only blocked requests were Google analytics/doubleclick beacons. No repository rule blocks the site's document, so no exception or replacement rule is needed — recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

No rule in the run instruction's filter policy blocks a fix here:⁠ the report is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing page, so rule generation was permitted and only the absence of a reproducible defect stopped it. The reported defect is a document-level block, so the fix would have been a scoped exception or a replacement rule; no filtering rule was found blocking anything the page needs.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

issue.title: gemini.google.com: exclude another Google Search selector that delays Copy
issue.body:
# Creating the pull request

## Prerequisites

- [x] This is not an ad/bug report;
- [x] My code follows the [guidelines](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [syntax](https://kb.adguard.com/general/how-to-create-your-own-ad-filters) of this project;
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own changes;
- [x] My changes do not break web sites, apps and files structure.

## What problem does the pull request fix?

- [x] Website or app doesn't work properly;

## What issue is being fixed?

Related: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/234825 (closed; same symptom, different selector)

1. Your comment

Same cause as #234825, which the comment above the existing Gemini exception describes: a `[style]` selector inside `:has()` makes Gemini's **Copy response** stall. The July fix excluded the `div[data-id="mosaic"]` rule. A second `google.*#?#` rule in `BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt` (`#search … span[style="padding:0 5px"]`) still applies on `gemini.google.com` and has the same effect.

This adds one `gemini.google.com#@#` exception for that exact selector, directly under the existing Gemini exception. The rule still applies on Google Search and every other `google.*` host.

Observed in Helium 0.20.1.1 (Chromium 156.0.8078.47) with uBlock Origin using AdGuard Base. Normal response Copy stalled with the rule and worked again after adding this exception and reloading (checked with a plain and a table response). We make no timing claim and do not test other Gemini actions here.

Validation:

- AGLint 4.0.0-beta.5 with the repository's `.aglintrc.yaml`: no problems.
- tsurlfilter 6.0.4 engine with `specific.txt` + this `allowlist.txt`: the rule no longer applies on `gemini.google.com`. It still applies on `www.google.com/search`, `www.google.de/search` and `docs.google.com`. No other element-hiding rule changes.

2. Screenshots

**Before — offending rule active**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83adf6ee-61c5-4a94-866a-d3536a1140d3

**After — Gemini-only exception enabled**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eeaad01c-a906-4602-8ff6-33463473df87

Synthetic normal Copy demonstration in Helium 0.20.1.1 with uBlock Origin and AdGuard Base. Before: the offending selector is active. After: the same response with the single Gemini-only exception enabled. Both clips preserve real time; editorial labels mark input and verified synthetic clipboard completion. One illustrative trial per condition, not a statistical speed comparison. This does not demonstrate a fix for Research Copy or Export to Docs.

### Terms

- [x] By submitting this issue, I agree that pull request does not contain private info and all conditions are met

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's screenshot shows the Crystal Mountain homepage's own "Ustawienia plików cookies" consent dialog dimming the page; it renders on first user interaction via the first-party `/cookie-monster/legacy.js` CMP and no existing filter covered it. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule `crystal-mountain.pl##.cm-container` was verified in the reporter's own settings profile (dialog gone, page intact, no residue), and belongs in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's specific-rules file. ## Rule `crystal-mountain.pl##.cm-container` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice annoyance, not one of the closed categories in the run instruction (no first-party advertising, no paywall, no anti-adblock wall), so no policy rule blocks a fix. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists precisely for this symptom; the fix is a domain-scoped element-hiding rule, the maintainers' preferred approach when hiding makes the page work (content unlocked, scrolling works, popup does not return). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3d8dc57420aaa480bd1483c70363a3f527fd0665/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40291852956 Automated analysis against filters at `3d8dc57`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — 2max.pl shows a first-party "gmgdpr" cookie-consent modal (#⁠gmgdpr-overlay) with a full-screen dark scrim that the Cookie Notices filter does not cover, even though the repository already hides the identical overlay on four other shops. Extending that shared rule with 2max.pl hides the modal and scrim with page integrity intact. ## Rule `2max.pl###gmgdpr-overlay` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice overlay, which the Annoyances filters exist to handle; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close/hand-off rules applies. Policy allows annoyance-filter rules for consent notices; the fix is a domain-scoped element hiding rule on a first-party modal id, with no JavaScript and no network blocking. The fix fits an existing shared multi-domain rule for the same #⁠gmgdpr-overlay element, so per the maintainer rule the reported domain is added to that rule rather than a new rule being written. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1b24bfc5e2433da4a9b38b9b9b9fbd9e24ef5415/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 5992](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1b24bfc5e2433da4a9b38b9b9b9fbd9e24ef5415/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L5992). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40291154024 Automated analysis against filters at `1b24bfc`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

issue.title: IDM “Download this video” Panel Disappears on YouTube When AdGuard Base Is Enabled

labels.name: A: Cannot reproduce
labels.description: Filters devs cannot reproduce this issue

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue;
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue.

### What product do you use?

AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version

AdGuard Browser extension Version 5.5.3.15

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Website or app doesn't work properly

### Which browser(s) do you use?

Chrome

### Which device do you use?

Desktop

### Where is the problem encountered?

https://www.youtube.com/

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

_No response_

### Social Widgets

_No response_

### Annoyances

_No response_

### Security

_No response_

### Other

_No response_

### DNS filters

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

I had a problem where the floating “Download this video” panel from Internet Download Manager (IDM) stopped appearing on YouTube videos in Chrome. IDM itself was working, but the download panel dI isappeared whenever AdGuard Base was enabled.

I spent some time testing my extensions and filters to find out what was causing it. Eventually, I narrowed the problem down to one specific scriptlet in the AdGuard Base filter.

My configuration

Google Chrome: 155.0.8059.85

IDM Integration Module: 6.43.1

AdGuard Base: Enabled

Other Chrome extensions were also enabled during the final test.

The suspected conflicting rule

I found this rule in my local adguard-base.txt file at line 46519:

youtube.com#%#//scriptlet('json-prune-fetch-response', 'playerResponse.adPlacements playerResponse.playerAds playerResponse.adSlots adPlacements playerAds adSlots', '', '/playlist\?list=|player\?|watch\?[tv]=/')

This scriptlet modifies JSON responses from certain YouTube Fetch requests by removing specified advertisement-related properties. In my testing, it appeared to interfere with the IDM download panel.

The workaround that fixed it for me

I opened AdGuard → Settings → User rules and added this exception:

youtube.com#@%#//scriptlet('json-prune-fetch-response', 'playerResponse.adPlacements playerResponse.playerAds playerResponse.adSlots adPlacements playerAds adSlots', '', '/playlist\?list=|player\?|watch\?[tv]=/')

I left AdGuard Base enabled and kept this exception as the only custom rule needed for the fix.

How I tested it

With AdGuard Base enabled and no exception, the IDM download panel disappeared.

I temporarily disabled all YouTube scriptlets using a broader exception, and the panel came back.

I tested an exception for the XHR response-pruning rule alone, but that did not restore the panel.

I then added the exception for the Fetch response-pruning rule. The IDM panel returned.

To make sure the XHR exception was not needed, I removed it and kept only the Fetch exception.

I completely closed and reopened Chrome, tested another YouTube video, and confirmed that the IDM download panel was still working.

I then enabled my other extensions, including uBlock Origin with EasyList, relaunched Chrome again, and confirmed that the panel continued to work.

Conclusion

In my setup, excluding the json-prune-fetch-response scriptlet restored the missing IDM download panel without disabling AdGuard Base or my other extensions.

I haven't established the exact internal reason why this rule interferes with IDM, but the result was reproducible in my testing.

Could the AdGuard filter maintainers please investigate whether this rule causes a compatibility issue with IDM's YouTube download-panel detection? A proper filter-side fix would be helpful for other users experiencing the same problem.

Workaround: Add the custom exception above under AdGuard User rules and keep AdGuard Base enabled.

I hope this helps anyone else who has the same issue.

### Privacy

- [x] #244860

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

tarnkappe.info shows a German anti-adblock wall ("Kein Bock auf Werbung? … Die Tarnkappe lässt sich nur ohne Werbeblocker lesen", only a link to instructions for disabling the blocker). The run instruction's filter policy says German anti-adblock walls get no rule and should be recommended for closing, so no rule is proposed.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing. This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it or to allowlist the site." The wall is on a German-language German site (html lang="de") and its text asks the user to disable the ad blocker:⁠ "Dieser Hinweis erscheint, weil du einen Werbeblocker verwendest. Die Tarnkappe lässt sich nur ohne Werbeblocker lesen." with the only control being "Anleitung zum Deaktivieren" linking to Chrome help for disabling extensions. The instruction states the agent never closes an issue; this outcome recommends closing for a maintainer to check and decide.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40290435366

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The "Gözden Kaçırma" recommendation overlay and the bottom-left Gleam consent card on bloomberght.com are rendered by the third-party gleams.dev module loader inside a shadow root, so element hiding cannot reach them. I propose the site-scoped network rule ||gleams.dev^$domain=bloomberght.com in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt, which apply_rule verified by blocking every gleams.dev request in the filtered phase. ## Rule `||gleams.dev^$domain=bloomberght.com` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No policy rule in the run instruction blocks this report:⁠ the symptom is a third-party vendor popup/consent overlay, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall. The page shows no ad-blocker detection and no anti-adblock wall; the annoyance is a vendor overlay rendered by a loadable third-party script visible in the network log, which the run instruction routes to a network rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c0a508db8283bfe64efa277a046f021915e63a18/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

### Add your comment and screenshots

Facebook/Meta appears to be generating an increasingly large number of `sonar` related `fbcdn.net` hostnames.

A collected set currently contains more than **7,000 individual Sonar hostnames**. please see the list here:

https://pastebin.com/TUPCjEG9


 Rather than being random one-off hosts, they follow several highly consistent naming families distributed across Meta's CDN locations.

The main observed patterns include:


sonar.<location>.fna.fbcdn.net
sonar6.<location>.fna.fbcdn.net

sonar-<location>.xx.fbcdn.net
sonar6-<location>.xx.fbcdn.net

edge-sonar-mini-shv-<node>-<location>.fbcdn.net
edge-sonar-mini6-shv-<node>-<location>.fbcdn.net


Examples:


sonar.faae1-1.fna.fbcdn.net
sonar6.faae1-1.fna.fbcdn.net

sonar-iad3-1.xx.fbcdn.net
sonar6-iad3-1.xx.fbcdn.net

edge-sonar-mini-shv-01-atl3.fbcdn.net
edge-sonar-mini6-shv-01-jnb2.fbcdn.net


There is direct evidence from Meta's own `facebook/dns` repository that these domains belong to a dedicated **Sonar** system rather than simply being ordinary static CDN hostnames.

Meta's DNS code contains an `isSonar()` function which identifies a hostname as Sonar when it:

1. ends in `.fbcdn.net`, and
2. contains `sonar` in the hostname.

It also separately recognizes WhatsApp's `.snr.whatsapp.net` Sonar-style domains.

Source:

https://github.com/facebook/dns/blob/9875b2096cd794d436e2af59609d61d5a61db371/dnsrocks/logger/utils.go

Meta's DNS logger also treats Sonar queries differently from ordinary DNS requests. The code explicitly states:

> We only sample non-sonar names

The relevant condition is:

```go
if localRand.Float64() > l.samplingRate && !isSonar(state) {
    return
}
```

This means requests classified as Sonar bypass the normal sampling exclusion applied to non-Sonar names and continue through the DNS logging path.

The logger records information including the query address, response address, query time, and DNS query message.

Source:

https://github.com/facebook/dns/blob/9875b2096cd794d436e2af59609d61d5a61db371/dnsrocks/logger/dnstap_logger.go

Meta's own tests also contain explicit Sonar hostname examples such as:

```text
f41366ce340-kdywlzry1535569283-sonar.xy.fbcdn.net
f41366ce340-kdywlzry1535569283-sonar.snr.fbcdn.net
f3d77e02580klz54ggi-uavvfioa1427990455-sonar.snr.fbcdn.net
fd45417ba30KDACNUXI-fgeytrfl1427990452-sonar.2914.fna.fbcdn.net
```

This confirms that these randomized-looking `*-sonar.*.fbcdn.net` hostnames are deliberately recognized as part of Meta's Sonar infrastructure.

Source:

https://github.com/facebook/dns/blob/9875b2096cd794d436e2af59609d61d5a61db371/dnsrocks/logger/dnstap_logger_test.go

Based on the available evidence, these hosts appear to be associated with **network telemetry, measurement, or diagnostics** rather than ordinary Facebook/Instagram image and video CDN delivery.

The scale is becoming difficult to handle using individual hostname rules. Thousands of location-specific Sonar hosts already exist, and additional CDN locations or node variants can generate more hostnames while retaining the same basic naming structure.

For that reason, I think it would make more sense to block the Sonar hostname family using a generic filtering rule

Conceptually:


suggested filter: * sonar * .fbcdn.net^


Interestingly, this is also very close to Meta's own internal detection logic, which considers an `.fbcdn.net` hostname containing `sonar` to be a Sonar domain.

A generic rule would target the dedicated Sonar infrastructure while avoiding a broad block of `fbcdn.net`, which could interfere with legitimate Facebook and Instagram CDN traffic.

I think these domains are strong candidates for classification as **Facebook/Meta telemetry or network-measurement endpoints** and for inclusion in the **AdGuard DNS filter**.


### Privacy

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On biznes.pwr.edu.pl the first-party "pressidium-cookie-consent" widget renders the "Witaj na stronach PWr" cookie dialog (body ⁠> #⁠cc--main ⁠> #⁠cc_div ⁠> #⁠cm) that no current rule handled. Adding the reported domain to the existing shared element-hiding rule for the same widget id (`###cc--main`) was verified in the reporter profile:⁠ dialog gone, page intact. ## Rule `biznes.pwr.edu.pl###cc--main` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, handled by the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter; it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's close rules apply. Filter policy for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter states that hiding the notice or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient in most cases; no feature gating was observed, so a plain element-hiding rule is within policy. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/45a6cf43788c87496d9825d269fd3801bdf30ad8/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 55](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/45a6cf43788c87496d9825d269fd3801bdf30ad8/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L55). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported anti-adblock overlay ("Wspieraj Bezpłatne Treści", "POWERED BY Admiral") reproduces on legnica.naszemiasto.pl and is rendered by the Admiral SDK loaded from agonyshark.com, so the fix is a network rule `||agonyshark.com^$domain=naszemiasto.pl` rather than element hiding. Both apply_rule experiments stopped in phase A because the main document returned HTTP 403, so the candidate could not be validated and is handed over for human review.

## Candidate for review

`||agonyshark.com^$domain=naszemiasto.pl`

PolishFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never judged the candidate:⁠ both experiments failed in phase A with phase_navigation_failed / http_blocked — 'Phase A navigation failed (http_blocked):⁠ main document returned HTTP 403' — so no before/after phases and no vision review ran, and the second answer marked the failure not retryable and directed an analysis-only finish. The candidate rests on the baseline session, where the overlay is present (reporterSymptomPresence:⁠ present) and the captured third-party requests show agonyshark.com serving the Admiral loader (artifact:⁠har:⁠4ad72932-9765-4977-8e7e-f92736f29903); it was not rejected, only unvalidated. A second, unverified risk for a human to weigh:⁠ pipsgain.com was also observed loading a bundle with the same build hash, so a mirror host might re-render the wall.

## Missing information

- Placement rule for Polish anti-adblock network rules (PolishFilter vs BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt): The run instruction and the linked guidance documents do not state which section file of the language-specific filter holds an anti-adblock network rule for a Polish site. `lookup_rule_guidance` (placement) only gives generic placement rules and the Base/Mobile/Experimental folder purposes, and `search_rules` shows no existing Admiral-family rule to copy a path from; the only evidence of a home for this site's rules is `PolishFilter/sections/specific.txt` (which holds `naszemiasto.pl#%#window.adBlockTest = true;`) and `BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt` (which holds the same scriptlet). The instruction's own anti-adblock example points at `BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt`, so the two candidates conflict and the choice was made from search results rather than from a documented placement rule.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://www.integraconsultores.com.ar/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.integraconsultores.com.ar%2F)

### Comment
> The domains integraconsultores.com.ar and www.integraconsultores.com.ar are blocked by AdGuard DNS as "malicious / phishing" (block page: "Access blocked by AdGuard DNS: Dangerous website"). I believe this is a false positive.
> 
> The site is the legitimate website of an Argentine consulting company (valuation and inventory of fixed assets).
> 
> Steps to reproduce:
> 1. Use the AdGuard DNS public servers (default): 94.140.14.14
> 2. Open https://www.integraconsultores.com.ar/
> 3. The block page is shown. A DNS lookup returns 94.140.14.33 (AdGuard block IP) instead of the real IP 67.227.154.94.
> 
> Checks done:
> - The domain resolves normally through Cloudflare 1.1.1.2, Quad9, OpenDNS and CleanBrowsing Security.
> - It is not listed in AdGuard DNS filter, Phishing Army, URLhaus, Dandelion Sprout anti-malware or Scam blocklist.
> - Sucuri SiteCheck (2026-10-26): no malware, no blacklists.
> 
> Please review it and remove the domain from the malicious/phishing database. Thank you!

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The "Adblocker detected" wall on lnbzi.com/9e166233ea reproduces in the reporter's profile (full-page vision of the current build:⁠ present) and in a default-lists profile, and is absent unfiltered; the page's own detector reports it (window.__tlm:⁠ detected=true, overlayShown=true). The overlay is engineered against cosmetic filtering (randomized custom element on <⁠html⁠>, closed shadow root, inline display:⁠block !important), and three evidence-based candidates — regex network block of the first-party overlay script, ExtendedCSS :⁠remove() of the overlay host, and abort-on-stack-trace on its insertion — each left the wall in place, so no rule could be verified.

## Still visible after the rule

- Verify Your Are Human. — A dark “Adblocker detected” modal is displayed over the page center, stating “We rely on ads to keep this site free. Please disable your adblocker for this domain and continue.” It includes “HOW TO DISABLE YOUR ADBLOCKER” instructions and buttons “I’ve disabled it” and “Reload page.” The modal overlays and obscures the white “Verify You Are Human” captcha card behind it, so the verification step is not accessible.
- Center of viewport, dark rounded panel headed 'Adblocker detected' with shield icon — Anti-adblock overlay blocking the page:⁠ 'We rely on ads to keep this site free. Please disable your adblocker for this domain and continue.' plus 'HOW TO DISABLE YOUR ADBLOCKER' list and 'I've disabled it' / 'Reload page' buttons. It sits on top of the white verification card and gates the visitor from proceeding.
- White ShrinkPe card behind the modal, captcha/'Verify You Are Human' step area with partially visible text 'Ple…ge.' — Gated verification content (captcha step and continue control) is covered by the adblock modal, so the destination link cannot be reached; the card's own content is obscured/withheld.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter-annotated element on https:⁠//blog.cloudflare.com/typescript-rust-port/ is the inline newsletter form ("Subscribe to receive notifications of new posts") served in the article HTML as section.post-email; it has no vendor loader request and no existing rule covers it. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule blog.cloudflare.com#⁠#⁠section.post-email verified in the locked AdGuard CLI baseline (symptom resolved, no remaining instances, page integrity intact) and is filed with the repository's other cloudflare.com subscription rules. ## Rule `blog.cloudflare.com##section.post-email` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules (first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls) do not apply:⁠ this is neither advertising nor a paywall, and the page shows no anti-adblock wall. The AdGuard filter policy document lists 'Popups and forms for subscribing to news, promotions, and various events' as a category the AdGuard Popups filter blocks, so a subscription-form rule is in scope. The form is first-party page HTML with no separate loader request, so the default fix is domain-scoped element hiding; no rule was copied from the issue (the issue carries only the comment 'subscription'). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3a7af09eff399eaa0f54bd491bccff99ec1c677c/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The antigravity.google download page builds its post-download survey pop-up from a template via the first-party chunk /_astro/DownloadSurvey*.js, which binds the click handler that opens the modal; the candidate `||antigravity.google/_astro/DownloadSurvey*` stops that loader. It could not be verified here because the pop-up only appears after clicking an external download link, which both interact_page and apply_rule refused as external_destination, and the vision review returned no verdict — so the rule is carried for human review.

## Candidate for review

`||antigravity.google/_astro/DownloadSurvey*`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt

Not verified: Both apply_rule experiments returned environmentExperiment 'inconclusive':⁠ the vision review produced no verdict ('Final vision synthesis failed after 3 attempts'), and the pop-up cannot appear in any phase because it is created only after a click on an external download link (storage.googleapis.com/antigravity-public/ or edgedl.me.gvt1.com/edgedl/). interact_page refused that click with 'external_destination', and the same click passed as revealSteps was refused in phases A, B and C (status 'refused', identical). The candidate was nonetheless applied by the engine in phase C (ruleApplications status 'applied') and absent in phase B, and no new page damage appeared; the blank bottom region was identical before and after.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's mid-article "Подписывайтесь на наш канал в MAX" strip on russiatoday.ru is the RT follows-channel component that AnnoyancesFilter already hides on russian.rt.com and three other sites; the domain-scoped rule russiatoday.ru#⁠#⁠.follows-channel was verified to hide it with page integrity intact, and the host merges it into that shared rule. ## Rule `russiatoday.ru##.follows-channel` ## Policy rationale The page shows no first-party ad creative:⁠ the residual advertising (banners.adfox.ru, smi2, 24smi, infox) is third-party and already blocked by the baseline Base/Russian filters, so the "site's own advertising" closure does not apply. No paywall and no anti-adblock wall is present, so those closure rules do not apply. The annotated promo strip is the same component the repository already hides as a subscription annoyance on russian.rt.com and three other sites; extending that shared rule is the repository's documented fix pattern ("When the fix fits an existing shared rule, add the reported domain to that rule"). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b8d79f76e9e8f786d5ce8d27a0342ddfb87fadb3/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 10123](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b8d79f76e9e8f786d5ce8d27a0342ddfb87fadb3/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt#L10123). ## Screenshots

labels.name: A: In progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue;
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue.

### What product do you use?

Other ad blocker

### AdGuard version

none

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Website or app doesn't work properly

### Which browser(s) do you use?

Firefox

### Which device do you use?

Desktop

### Where is the problem encountered?

https://www.globalcitizensolutions.com/

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

_No response_

### Social Widgets

_No response_

### Annoyances

AdGuard Annoyances filter

### Security

_No response_

### Other

_No response_

### DNS filters

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

Send Do-Not-Track signals

### Add your comment and screenshots

The content on the website is not clickable/selectable due to the presence of `gcs-cc-lock` class on `<html>`, causing the `html.gcs-cc-lock body::before` rule to cover the page with a transparent `::before` pseudo-element. The `gcs-cc-lock` class is usually removed by accepting the cookie consent. However, since the consent is removed by the following rule, that does not occur: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c674b6c7e2d7f265e5f12d7e9c06df5f750724d5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_general.txt#L272

Adding `globalcitizensolutions.com##+js(remove-class, gcs-cc-lock, html)` effectively avoids the issue.

### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body: Thanks for addressing this issue so quickly @ntnguyen1234!  Good thought to block the whole Wordpress plugin.  Unfortunately, after updating and testing in a fresh Firefox profile, I'm still seeing the same issue.  The logger shows that `https://www.globalcitizensolutions.com/wp-content/plugins/gdpr-cookie-compliance/dist/scripts/main.js?ver=5.2.2` is blocked by the updated rule, but `gcs-cc-lock` is still left on `<html>` after loading, blocking clicks and selection.  Can you take another look?

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — foxnews.com's "Welcome to Fox News!" ad-block wall is Admiral's platform, loaded as third-party scripts from technonstop.com; blocking that host for the reported site removed the wall and left the page readable in the verified A/B experiment. Proposed:⁠ ||technonstop.com^$domain=foxnews.com in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt. ## Rule `||technonstop.com^$domain=foxnews.com` ## Policy rationale The wall is not a German anti-adblock wall, so the German-wall close rule does not apply. The captured requests show the detector/loader scripts (technonstop.com, thirdParty, HTTP 200) that render the Admiral wall, satisfying the policy branch 'write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script'. The wall overlays and dims essentially the entire homepage, insists on disabling the ad blocker and offers no route to the content, which the filter policy lists as a blockable anti-adblock wall. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b53c8ce0d0f7af2bb20c1262ce5d76a8d7a5a17a/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40362472867 Automated analysis against filters at `b53c8ce`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"bc5db20169d4b0d78a47178f015bdb030405c46c13b291578f4aa574609d7d98"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The benq.com cookie banner is already hidden in the filtered baseline and the page scrolls normally (scrollY reached 4620 of 5700) even though body still carries `overflow: hidden`, so the reported scroll lock did not reproduce. The reporter's banner-visible consent state (the page declares memberRegion=Non-EU) was unreachable without a geo route, and no cosmetic rule could be attributed, so no rule is proposed.

## Missing information

- No unfiltered control session and no cosmetic-rule attribution in the adguard_cli route: For issue #⁠245469 (benq.com, incorrect blocking) I needed to diff an unfiltered page against the prepared baseline and to name the rule that hides the site's cookie banner. Neither was available in the locked adguard_cli environment:⁠ (1) launch_browser refused `settings` on an `extension:"none"` session and stated that a control session "runs no blocker", but every session in this route still browses through the AdGuard CLI filtering proxy (local.adguard.org content-script and Tracking Protection scriptlets were injected in the `extension:"none"` session), so no genuinely unfiltered capture was obtainable. (2) `get_applied_rules` for the AdGuard CLI engine reported only 4 Tracking Protection scriptlet rules and explicitly does not report extended-CSS (`#?#`) hiding, so the element-hiding rule behind the hidden `.cookie-bar` could not be identified, and `search_rules` shows no benq.com rule and no generic `.cookie-bar` rule in this repository. A run on this route therefore cannot attribute a cosmetic hide or provide an unfiltered/prepared diff.

## Artifacts

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — debatte.bild.de loads the third-party Ad-Shield anti-adblock SDK from html-load.com and then sends the top frame to https:⁠//www⁠.bild.de/adblockwall.html, which filtering blocks, leaving visitors on a "www⁠.bild.de is blocked" error page instead of the debates content. The candidate rule extending the repository's Ad-Shield html-load.com family with debatte.bild.de could not be judged because the experiment's phase C navigation was destroyed by that same site redirect, so it is handed over unverified.

## Candidate for review

`||html-load.com^$script,xmlhttprequest,domain=debatte.bild.de`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule could not judge the candidate:⁠ phases A and B loaded https:⁠//debatte.bild.de/ but phase C failed with "Navigation did not complete after 3 attempts:⁠ https:⁠//debatte.bild.de/ (page.evaluate:⁠ Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation)", so environmentExperiment is inconclusive, validationSkipped is true and no visual review verdict was produced. Separately, the run instruction's German anti-adblock wall policy could not be applied or excluded because the wall page itself is blocked by the baseline and no unfiltered observation is possible in adguard_cli.

## Missing information

- Reporter screenshot artifact not registered for issue #⁠245471: fetch_issue returned an empty issueScreenshots array, and analyze_screenshot(issueScreenshotIndex=1) answered "Reporter screenshot index 1 is unavailable" with availableIssueScreenshotIndices:⁠ [⁠]⁠. The body only links https:⁠//cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/tiwh2oiuhuswcsows80owsc444co880mpht97gswzk.jpg?nc=1, which the browser refuses to open ("URL must remain on configured issue origin 'https:⁠//debatte.bild.de'"). The reporter-defined target (the annotated defect) therefore could not be inspected.
- No unfiltered observation possible in adguard_cli; the site's wall page cannot be read: Every browser session in the locked adguard_cli environment goes through the filtering proxy, so there is no unfiltered control view. On debatte.bild.de the site navigates the top frame to https:⁠//www⁠.bild.de/adblockwall.html, which the baseline blocks (ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT), so the wall page's own text — needed to decide whether the run instruction's "German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule" rule applies (it requires a wall that "asks to disable it or to allowlist the site") — could not be observed. Opening www⁠.bild.de is refused as off-origin.
- search_rules urlPattern cannot be enumerated; blocking rule for www⁠.bild.de/adblockwall.html not found: search_rules with urlPattern only returns a rule when the query equals the rule's pattern text (e.g. "||asadcdn.com/adlib/*.js" matched, "asadcdn.com/adlib" did not; a rule that exists with modifiers, "||asadcdn.com/adlib/pages/sport1.js$domain=sport1.de", did not match even verbatim). Exact probes for ||bild.de/adblockwall.html, ||www⁠.bild.de/adblockwall.html (with and without ^ and $document) returned 0 matches, and get_detail on the domain inventory truncates at \~7 KB before the network matches, so the rule that blocks the wall document could not be identified. get_applied_rules could not be used either:⁠ it refuses while the session's page is the chrome-error page the redirect leaves behind.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On datanodes.to the live page reproduces the report (premium promos plus a "STEP 1 OF 2" interstitial before the file), and two cosmetic candidates removed the promos and the step label with page integrity intact, but the vision review refused both because the download itself still needs a click on the server-controlled "Continue to Download" interstitial. No single rule could be verified, and the site's existing datanodes.to self-promo and trusted-click-element rules are stale against the new layout.

## Still visible after the rule

- File Ready panel — 'Continue to Download' button — The page is a 'preliminary check' interstitial:⁠ after the 'File Ready / Verified and ready to download' panel and a 4/4 complete progress list, the user must still click the blue 'Continue to Download' button to reach the actual file. This is the extra gating click that matches the reporter's 'twice or thrice click to actually download' symptom. No countdown timer and no premium/promo upsell line is visible in this state.
- Large blue 'Continue to Download' button centered at the bottom of the white download card, below the 'verified content partner' notice — Intermediate action button standing between the visitor and the actual file:⁠ the download is not delivered on page load but requires this extra click, matching the reporter's 'twice or thrice click to actually download file'.

## Missing information

- Reporter screenshots for issue #⁠245472 are not available as artifacts: fetch_issue returned an empty `issueScreenshots` array, although the issue body links three reporter screenshots (cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/76170ujmdk84cc8kokws8w8gcg84gcc29uejyitftu.png, .../4ksb6emqao0048sw04kk8ook0sgs4cor8gim8sctmo.png, .../ihdkzsckcp44wsogsw4oksgcs08s8gqxzqmp5fgg00.png). Because no screenshot artifact ID exists, analyze_screenshot cannot be used and the reporter-defined target (including any annotation) had to be inferred from the live page only. The run instruction makes the reporter screenshot the primary definition of the defect, so this is a real targeting gap for this report.

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

### What product do you use?

AdGuard Content Blocker

Adguard Popup Blocker 2.5.117

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Annoyances — pop-ups, cookie warnings, etc.

Safari

Desktop

AdGuard Base filter

AdGuard URL Tracking filter

AdGuard Social Media filter

AdGuard Popups filter

Online Malicious URL Blocklist

AdGuard Experimental filter

_No response_

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

1. On thegatewaypundit.com site, with Adguard Popups and Adguard popup blocker both enabled, I still periodically see a large full-page popup or overlay that prompts "Please disable your ad blocker."

2. I believe this is happening because Adtoniq is not being filtered out.  By comparison, run Firefox v.157 with Ublock Origin on my Mac, and it DOES properly filter this popup out.  Their list does filter Adtoniq. 



### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body:
Understood, no worries.  Appreciate your time here. 

I just wish I could figure out why this all seems to work flawlessly with Firefox + Ublock origin (didn't have to configure a thing, just use UBO with its normal lists and this popup gets blocked), or Brave with its internal "Shields" (same thing, just use the shields/lists, I never see this popup).   It only seems to happen in one use case:  Using Safari (MacOS 27 or iOS 27), with the Wblock extension, and using all the Adguard lists/filters that are included with Wblock.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bazel.build shows a "We value your privacy" c15t cookie-consent banner pinned bottom-left over the page; the first-party ConsentManager loader blocks badly (page rendered blank), so the verified fix is the cosmetic rule bazel.build#⁠#⁠[⁠data-testid="consent-banner-root"]⁠, which removes the banner with page integrity intact. ## Rule `bazel.build##[data-testid="consent-banner-root"]` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance ('Annoyance' issue type, comment 'cookie') on bazel.build — not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is designed to hide cookie notices and CMP UI, and hiding the notice is sufficient here:⁠ nothing on the page is gated, and the verified candidate leaves the page intact. No existing shared or vendor rule covers c15t/Mintlify consent UI, so a new site-scoped rule is required rather than an extension of an existing family. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4ac66dfa5f2e404ec415f86a89a24ff7517737ed/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Fixable by using the Reader Mode browser feature, disabling JavaScript in browser or blocking JavaScript for the site using filter rules. Disabling JavaScript improves page loading times at the cost of site functionality; it's fine for just reading.

In this example, replace `example.com` with the corresponding domain then add to custom rules:
```adblock
*$script,third-party,domain=example.com
||example.com^$script
||example.com^$inline-script
```

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The blocked MicroAd Compass footer slot on the reported Seesaa wiki leaves an empty 300x250 div that paints a \~250px blank gap between the 最近更新したページ and アクセス数の多いページ panels. A reported-domain-scoped element-hiding rule for that leftover container was verified with apply_rule (symptom resolved, gap 260px→10px section margin, page integrity intact). ## Rule `anothereden.game-info.wiki###footer-contents > div[style^="width:300px"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction states no policy rule that closes this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock wall at all. The defect is an empty reserved ad container left by a blocked third-party MicroAd loader — a removable annoyance leftover, not first-party advertising content, so a rule may be generated. The rule hides only the empty container; the ad request itself is already blocked/redirected by the existing Japanese filter rule and is not changed. ## Place in the list [MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/fcce0171c3e51447d0e45d8c4060c939f952acac/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Issue #⁠245481 screenshot not available as a registered artifact: fetch_issue returned issueScreenshots:⁠ [⁠]⁠ for issue #⁠245481, although the issue body embeds a screenshot at https:⁠//cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/bnkqt943swg8ws440wk4so44k4cooswry9zmmk2ljk.jpg?nc=1. Because no artifact ID or issue screenshot index exists, analyze_screenshot cannot inspect the reporter's annotated target, so the reporter-defined defect must be identified from the issue text and live page evidence instead. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — deeplol.gg's summoner page leaves two blocked-ad leftovers:⁠ an empty light-gray 430x230 ad placeholder filling the right half of the profile header card, and a 350px-tall empty banner container in the left column that opens a visible gap. One domain-scoped hiding rule removed both in the A/B/C experiment (gap gone, document 2171→1762px, page integrity intact), but the vision review still counted the header card's own blank background as ad residue, so the rule is carried for human review.

## Candidate for review

`deeplol.gg##.p__info > div:has(> div:not([class]):only-child:empty), div:has(> div > a[target="_blank"] > img[src^="./images/ad/"])`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: visualReview verdict rejected with adLayoutResidue present, pageIntegrity intact and observedDamage empty:⁠ both reported leftovers (the 430x230 rgb(217,217,217) header ad box and the 350px empty banner container in the left column) went from visible to hidden, the left-column gap was accepted as resolved, but the review still counted the blank right half of the profile header card as residue. domChecks measured that space:⁠ .p__info paints its own rgb(38,38,38) background, holds no [⁠data-ad]⁠/iframe/ins, is 1080px wide like #⁠summoner_content_box, and after the candidate its only laid-out child is the 1078px summoner-info block (ad box display:⁠none, 0x0) — the blank is the page's own header layout, which no #⁠#⁠ rule can collapse; a #⁠$#⁠ rule to shrink the card is barred because the bound #⁠#⁠ review reported no page-integrity regression.

## Still visible after the rule

- TILE 1, Document y=0..1080 — summoner profile header row, right side beside the vuri #⁠DMS name/rank card — Large empty reserved area filling the right side of the summoner profile header card beside the name, avatar, and rank content. No ad creative, advertising label, divider, or placeholder block is visible in it, matching the reported blocked-ad leftover.
- Summoner profile header row, right side beside the vuri#⁠DMS name/rank card — Large blank region occupying the right portion of the profile header card; no ad creative, REKLAMA label, divider, frame, or placeholder block is visible in it.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — mobileasia.com.pl shows a persistent first-party RODO cookie-consent panel fixed across the bottom of the viewport that no enabled filter blocks; a domain-scoped element-hiding rule anchored on the panel's cookie icon hides it and was verified with page integrity intact. The reporter's screenshot could not be retrieved, so the target was identified from live page evidence rather than the annotation. ## Rule `mobileasia.com.pl##div.fixed.bottom-0:has(svg.lucide-cookie)` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice on a shop page:⁠ not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall (no detector request in the captured network log and no gated content; pageObstruction none), so no policy rule closes it. The German anti-adblock-wall exclusion does not apply:⁠ the page is Polish and shows no ad-blocker detection message.
